git clone https://github.com/ultralytics/yolov5
cd yolov5
pip install -r requirements.txt

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: YOLOv5 is a fast, accurate computer vision model from Ultralytics, built on PyTorch. It detects objects in images and video, and also supports instance segmentation and image classification, with pretrained models you can use straight away or train on your own data.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building an object detector from scratch takes research skills and lots of compute. YOLOv5 gives you pretrained models, ready-made scripts for inference and training, and export to deployment formats like ONNX and TensorRT.
whoFor: Developers adding object detection to apps
Students and hobbyists learning computer vision
Teams training detectors on custom datasets
Engineers deploying models to edge devices
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature, production-proven detector with simple scripts. For the latest models, the README points to the newer ultralytics package (pip install ultralytics).
requirements: A GPU is recommended for training

overview: YOLOv5 comes in five sizes, from yolov5n (nano) to yolov5x (extra large), trading speed for accuracy. Pretrained weights download automatically from the latest release the first time you use them.

You can run it through PyTorch Hub with a few lines of Python, or with the detect.py script, which accepts images, videos, folders, webcams, screen captures, YouTube links and RTSP streams and saves results to runs/detect. train.py trains on datasets such as COCO, and export.py converts models to formats like ONNX, TensorRT, CoreML and TFLite.

Release v7.0 added instance segmentation models with their own scripts in the segment folder. YOLOv5 is AGPL-3.0 licensed; Ultralytics offers an Enterprise License for commercial use that can't meet AGPL terms.

tutorial.title: Detect objects in a photo with PyTorch Hub
tutorial.useCase: Load a pretrained YOLOv5 model in Python and run it on an image.

steps.title: Load the model and run inference
steps.code:
import torch

model = torch.hub.load("ultralytics/yolov5", "yolov5s")
img = "https://ultralytics.com/images/zidane.jpg"
results = model(img)

tutorial.expected: The model downloads automatically, prints the detected objects, shows the annotated image and saves it to runs/detect/exp.
